concepts.name: Structural Composition of CPI vs WPI Baskets
key_dimensions: Weight of food articles in CPI (~45-46%) vs WPI (~24%) and policy implications
Services inclusion in CPI but complete exclusion from WPI
Manufactured products dominate WPI (~64%) but are minor in CPI
UPSC trap: WPI does not capture services inflation at all, unlike CPI

concepts.name: Base Year Differences and Recent Revisions
key_dimensions: Current base year: CPI (2012) vs WPI (2011-12) and rationale for periodic revision
Items added/removed during last revision — e.g., new manufacturing items in WPI 2011-12
Impact of base year choice on measured inflation rates
UPSC trap: Both indices were revised around similar periods but have different base years

concepts.name: Compiling Agencies and Institutional Responsibility
key_dimensions: CPI compiled by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) — National Statistical Office
WPI compiled by Office of the Economic Adviser (OEA), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
RBI's formal shift from WPI to CPI for monetary policy targeting (2014 Urjit Patel Committee recommendation)
UPSC trap: RBI uses CPI, not WPI, as the nominal anchor for inflation targeting

concepts.name: CPI Variants: CPI-IW, CPI-AL, CPI-RL, and CPI-Combined
key_dimensions: CPI-IW (Industrial Workers) compiled by Labour Bureau — used for Dearness Allowance (DA) calculation
CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers) and CPI-RL (Rural Labourers) — used for minimum wage revision
CPI-Combined (Urban + Rural) — used by RBI for inflation targeting
UPSC trap: DA for central government employees is linked to CPI-IW, NOT CPI-Combined

concepts.name: Price Stage Captured: Producer vs Consumer Level
key_dimensions: WPI measures prices at the first point of commercial transaction (producer/wholesale level)
CPI measures prices at the retail level — final consumer stage
WPI as a leading indicator of future retail inflation through the supply chain
UPSC trap: WPI can be negative even when CPI is positive — deflation at wholesale, inflation at retail

concepts.name: Inflation Targeting Framework and CPI's Legal Mandate
key_dimensions: RBI Act amendment (2016) — Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework formalized CPI as target
Target: 4% CPI with ±2% tolerance band (2-6%)
Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) mandate — CPI breach for 3 consecutive quarters triggers RBI report to govt
UPSC trap: The target is CPI-Combined (all-India), not any sectoral CPI variant

concepts.name: WPI as a Deflator and Its Use in GDP Calculation
key_dimensions: WPI historically used as deflator for manufacturing sector in GDP estimation
Shift towards use of CPI and PPI (Producer Price Index) in national accounts
Difference between GDP deflator and WPI — GDP deflator is broader
UPSC trap: GDP deflator ≠ WPI; GDP deflator covers all goods and services including exports/imports

concepts.name: Divergence Between CPI and WPI: Causes and Implications
key_dimensions: Supply chain margins, taxes, and transportation costs cause CPI > WPI typically
Scenarios where WPI exceeds CPI — commodity price spikes (crude oil, metals) not yet passed to consumers
Negative WPI with positive CPI — deflation in traded goods but sticky retail prices (e.g., 2015-16 episode)
UPSC trap: Divergence signals either supply chain inefficiency or administered price mechanisms

concepts.name: Frequency and Data Release Timelines
key_dimensions: WPI released monthly with a shorter lag (~2 weeks after month end)
CPI released monthly — typically 12-14 days after month end by MoSPI
WPI data undergoes two revisions (provisional → first revision → final)
UPSC trap: WPI data is revised twice; CPI data revision process differs — important for policy timing

concepts.name: Treatment of Imports and Traded Commodities in WPI vs CPI
key_dimensions: WPI includes imported commodities at wholesale price — directly reflects global price shocks
CPI does not separately track import prices — captures only what consumers pay finally
Crude oil price spike impacts WPI faster; CPI impact is delayed due to retail price stickiness
UPSC trap: WPI is more sensitive to global commodity cycles than CPI

concepts.name: Absence of Services in WPI — A Critical Structural Gap
key_dimensions: WPI covers only goods — primary articles, fuel & power, manufactured products
Services like education, health, rent, transport constitute ~50%+ of CPI weight
WPI understates overall price pressure in a services-dominated economy like modern India
UPSC trap: India's economy is services-led, making WPI increasingly less representative of actual inflation

concepts.name: Food Inflation Measurement: Differences in Scope and Weight
key_dimensions: CPI food basket includes vegetables, cereals, pulses, milk, spices with high weight (~45%)
WPI food articles include primary food + processed food but with lower combined weight
Core CPI excludes food and fuel — used to assess demand-side inflation
UPSC trap: High food weight in CPI means a bad monsoon raises CPI sharply but WPI moderately

concepts.name: Core Inflation vs Headline Inflation in CPI Context
key_dimensions: Headline CPI = all items; Core CPI = CPI excluding food and fuel/energy
RBI uses headline CPI for targeting but monitors core CPI for demand-side pressures
No equivalent 'core WPI' concept is used in Indian policy discourse
UPSC trap: WPI has no formal 'core' counterpart used in RBI communications

concepts.name: Rural vs Urban Inflation Dynamics in CPI
key_dimensions: CPI-Combined = weighted average of CPI-Rural (weight ~55%) and CPI-Urban (~45%)
Rural CPI typically higher due to food price sensitivity and supply constraints
WPI has no rural/urban disaggregation — single national wholesale price index
UPSC trap: UPSC often tests whether students know the rural weight in CPI is higher than urban

concepts.name: Producer Price Index (PPI) as a Proposed Replacement for WPI
key_dimensions: PPI recommended by multiple committees (Abhijit Sen Working Group) to replace WPI
PPI measures prices received by domestic producers — excludes indirect taxes unlike WPI
PPI better aligned with international standards (UN, IMF recommendations)
UPSC trap: India has NOT yet officially switched to PPI — WPI still in use as of 2024

concepts.name: Impact of Taxes and Subsidies on WPI vs CPI Measurement
key_dimensions: WPI includes indirect taxes (GST, excise) in the price — not a pure producer price
CPI retail prices include all taxes, margins, and distribution costs
PPI proposed to exclude taxes to isolate pure producer price signal
UPSC trap: WPI ≠ PPI because WPI includes taxes; a common misconception that WPI = producer prices net of taxes

concepts.name: Dearness Allowance (DA) Linkage and Wage Indexation
key_dimensions: DA for central government employees and pensioners linked to CPI-IW (base year 2016)
Minimum wages for agricultural workers revised using CPI-AL
WPI has no direct wage indexation role in India's current framework
UPSC trap: The 7th Pay Commission and DA calculations use CPI-IW, not CPI-Combined or WPI

concepts.name: Seasonal Adjustment and Volatility Differences
key_dimensions: CPI is highly seasonal due to high food weight — kharif/rabi harvest cycles affect readings significantly
WPI also seasonal but manufacturing component provides some smoothing
RBI uses seasonally adjusted and 3-month moving average data for policy decisions
UPSC trap: Seasonal food price spikes in CPI may not warrant rate hikes if core inflation is stable

concepts.name: Historical Policy Shift: From WPI to CPI as Monetary Policy Anchor
key_dimensions: Pre-2014: RBI informally targeted WPI for monetary policy — legacy of goods-dominated economy
Urjit Patel Committee Report (2014) recommended CPI as nominal anchor
Rationale: CPI better reflects household welfare, consumption basket, and services
UPSC trap: The shift was recommended by Urjit Patel Committee, NOT the Narasimham Committee or Chakravarty Committee

concepts.name: Number of Items Tracked: Coverage Breadth Comparison
key_dimensions: WPI tracks ~697 items across three major groups (primary articles, fuel, manufactured goods)
CPI tracks ~299 items but with broader household expenditure coverage including services
More items in WPI does not mean better consumer welfare measurement — composition matters
UPSC trap: WPI covers more items numerically, but CPI is considered superior for policy due to service coverage
